title: Thrift Mode: Adaptive inference playbook for micro-batching, hybrid cache tiers, and quant profiles
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: Create an operational playbook and rollout plan that captures a repeatable, low-risk path to per-token savings using three levers: micro-batching heuristics, hybrid cache tiering (hot prefix + warm KV layers), and conservative quantization profiles. The playbook will include measurement artifacts, gating criteria, automated rules for runtime selection, and a set of trial cohorts for production experiments. Scope excludes model architecture changes; focuses on serving/runtime knobs, console controls, and evaluation/rollback automation.

2026-03-16: Micro-batching prototype & server-side config flags merged (ENG PR #4521)

success_metrics: >10% reduction in per-token CPU/GPU cost for targeted routes within trial cohorts
Median p99 latency regression <= 5% after applying micro-batching and cache tiers
Adoption: at least 3 product routes adopt Thrift Mode in first quarter post-launch
No undetected quality regressions (delta Bleu/ROUGE/LL decrease within pre-defined tolerances)
risks: Quality regressions from quantization on edge prompt types; mitigation: guarded profile and eval set gating
Complexity of cache eviction across multi-tenant hot/warm tiers; mitigation: RBAC and per-customer TTLs in design
Autoscale interactions causing transient increased latency with larger micro-batch windows; mitigation: dynamic windowing tied to real-time SLO signals
